data.reasoning: The only complete, non-advisory report (deepseek-v4-flash) found the PKGBUILD to be a standard Rust application build with no malicious indicators. The source is pinned with sha256sum from the official GitHub repository, build uses standard cargo commands with locked/frozen flags, and installation follows normal Arch packaging patterns. The other two reports either had tool errors (qwen3-235b) or were marked advisory-only (openrouter/free), providing no valid verdict signal per the adjudication rules.
data.disagreement_analysis: The apparent disagreement was between tool failures and a successful analysis. Report 1 (qwen3-235b) suffered HTTP 400 API errors on PKGBUILD and LICENSE, Report 3 (openrouter/free) had an LLMResponseError on LICENSE and was marked advisory-only. Neither provides a valid verdict signal. Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) completed successfully and found no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507: API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) prevented review of PKGBUILD and LICENSE files
openrouter/free: LLMResponseError prevented review of LICENSE file
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, LLM response errors) should trigger automatic retry or fallback to prevent inconclusive verdicts when the package itself may be safe
Advisory reports should be excluded from verdict calculation entirely, not just downweighted, to avoid confusion in disagreement detection
When multiple reports fail with tool errors on the same files, the audit system should recognize this as a systemic issue rather than treating each failure independently
